sections.h2: Hazard offices for Perry County property tax
sections.html:
Everything a seller needs is in Hazard. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values parcels on an upper floor of the courthouse at 481 Main Street, and the County Clerk sits on the ground floor. Bills are mailed and collected by the Sheriff's Office on East Main Street.

  • Sheriff's tax office: 124 East Main Street; letters go to box 7309, Hazard 41702. It is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:00 except holidays. The number is 606-439-4523, option 2.
  • PVA: 606-436-4914. A link to the PVA's parcel search sits on the sheriff's tax page.
  • County Clerk: 606-436-4614.

Checks to the sheriff are made payable to "Perry County Sheriff." A separate billing provider handles online payment and adds its own convenience fee.

Perry County runs on the standard Kentucky calendar from KRS 134.015.

Perry County payment calendar
When you payWhat applies
By November 12% discount for paying in full
Through the end of DecemberAmount on the bill
January5% penalty
After January 3110% penalty
Close of business April 15Sheriff's collection year ends

Mailing dates shift from year to year, so call the tax office at 606-439-4523 to confirm the dates printed on your bill. The sheriff collects state, county and district taxes, and earns a commission on the collections. In a year when bills go out late, each stage lasts a full month instead.

You can pay in person at 124 East Main Street on weekdays, 8:00 to 4:00, holidays excepted. For a mailed payment, make the check out to "Perry County Sheriff" and send it to box 7309, Hazard 41702. Online payment goes through a separate billing provider that charges its own convenience fee, so a check or a counter payment costs less. If something about the bill looks wrong, call 606-439-4523 and press option 2 before you pay, and ask the PVA at 606-436-4914 about any question of value.

Save the receipt, because the buyer's title company will want proof of payment or a figure to prorate.

Every month of delinquency adds cost. Any bill open after April 15 shifts to the County Clerk, where one percent monthly interest and clerk and attorney commissions begin to accrue. A clerk's sale follows 90 to 135 days after the transfer.

The County Clerk's website points to a delinquent tax application, and the county attorney's office can set up an installment plan on a current delinquency. If you are selling, ask for a payoff in writing, because the balance changes every month the bill stays open.

sections.h2: Can a Perry County owner contest the value?
sections.html: Yes. Begin at the PVA's office and meet with staff before filing anything. Next, deliver the written appeal to the clerk's desk by the end of the day after the thirteen-day roll inspection closes. A local board of neighbors hears it, generally within five weeks, and it weighs hard evidence such as appraisals, repair bids and nearby sales. Bring photos of any defects the PVA may not know about.

A homeowner who is 65 or older, or who is classed as totally disabled, can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026.

Bring a birth certificate, license or other proof of age when you apply,.

sections.h2: What a seller pays to record a deed
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax falls on the grantor. Under KRS 142.050 it is a half dollar per $500 of the price on the deed, a partial $500 counted as whole, and the clerk takes it before accepting the instrument. The Perry County Clerk's published minimums are $50 for a deed and $80 for a mortgage, and a deed adds $3 for each page after the fifth.

Expect the title company to ask for three things: proof that the current bill is paid or prorated, a payoff from the clerk when an earlier year went delinquent, and an in-care-of address on the deed. Clerk staff will quote a total on any document but will not search titles, so hire an attorney or abstractor for that.

Perry County is an inexpensive market. A typical owned home is valued at $91,800, owners occupy 70.4% of homes, and the household income midpoint is $42,181.

  • The 2025 estimate of 26,555 people is 6.7% below the 2020 count of 28,473.
  • Median rent is $798. An owner with a mortgage spends $1,167 monthly and one without spends $379.
  • The 2020 census found 13,213 housing units, 13.1% vacant. By 2025 the count was 13,425 units, and no building permits were issued.

With a falling population and many empty units, price carefully and be ready to show the condition of the house.

sections.h2: Setting and taxes for business sellers
sections.html:
About 343 square miles of Appalachian coalfield make up Perry County, whose only incorporated cities are Hazard and Buckhorn. Two school systems, Perry County Schools and Hazard Independent Schools, serve homes here, so know which one covers your address.

Perry County also levies an occupational license tax of 1% on wages and net profit, and people who work inside Hazard pay both the county and the city. If you are selling a rental or commercial building, ask an accountant how that affects you.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed, step by step
sections.html:
A delinquent year does not stop a sale. What you need is the exact payoff and a plan to clear it at closing.

  1. Locate the bill: the sheriff holds it until April 15, and the County Clerk holds it after.
  2. Request a written payoff. Interest and commissions change monthly.
  3. For a large debt, the county attorney's office can discuss an installment plan on a current delinquency.
  4. Hand the payoff to the title company for payment out of your proceeds.
  5. Verify that a release was recorded, and file a copy.

A cash purchase means no waiting on a buyer's loan or appraisal. The tax debt gets paid at closing regardless. Handle it early, and the rest of the sale is simpler.

sections.h2: Phone calls to make before you list
sections.html:
Three short calls will save a seller time. Ring the sheriff's tax office at 606-439-4523, option 2, and ask whether the current bill is paid and whether anything older is outstanding. Call the PVA at 606-436-4914 and ask what value and classification are on the roll for your parcel. Then call the clerk at 606-436-4614 and ask whether a certificate of delinquency or any other lien is recorded against the house.

Write down the name of whoever you speak with, the date and the figure you were quoted, and pass those notes to the closing agent. A clear record at all three counters makes the title work simpler.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Perry County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Go to the Sheriff's Office at 124 East Main Street in Hazard, open weekdays 8:00 to 4:00. To pay by mail, use box 7309 and make the check out to Perry County Sheriff.

faqs.q: How much does the homestead exemption take off a Perry County home?
faqs.a: It subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026 if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. Get the form from the PVA.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Perry County sale?
faqs.a: Sellers pay fifty cents per $500 of the deed's stated price, collected by the clerk ahead of recording.

faqs.q: Where do unpaid Perry County bills go after April 15?
faqs.a: The county clerk receives them as certificates of delinquency, and one percent monthly interest starts, plus clerk and attorney fees.

faqs.q: Who decides a Perry County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: A local board made up of area property owners. You meet the PVA first, then file with the clerk no later than the workday after inspection ends.
